---
title: "Figure 5 by instrumental noise — distortion versus the memory left in the least-squares residual"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
WRITTEN 2026-08-11 (Luciano). Fourth encoding of the same 840 marks as figure_5.Rmd, and the third
of the three that put ONE design axis on the rows. Here it is the INSTRUMENTAL NOISE. Column =
member, row = S_tilde, colour = the acquisition interval, and the channel count is not drawn.
The companion is figure_5_Nch.Rmd, which puts the channel count on the rows instead; the body figure
puts the sampling interval there. Between the three, every design axis has had its turn as the row.

THE NOISE IS THE LABEL DIVIDED BY TEN. S_tilde = label/10, noise_units.R, and it is converted here
because here is where it is shown. The nine rows are clean decades, 10^-2 to 10^6, which is why this
particular axis makes a legible set of rows: the three levels of the spectrum file that are not
decades (labels 0.05, 0.2, 0.5) have no lag in cell_scalars and were already dropped by the join in
every version of this figure.

THE ROWS ARE A STAIRCASE AND THAT IS THE BATTERY, NOT A LOSS. The design does not cross noise with
channel count fully: the highest noises were only run at the largest patches (S_tilde 10^4 at every
channel count, 10^5 from N_ch = 100 up, 10^6 only at N_ch = 10^4), so the bottom rows carry fewer
marks than the top ones. Counts per row are printed by the data chunk. Nothing is filtered here.

WHAT THIS ENCODING IS FOR. Within a row two things still move a mark, the sampling rate which is the
colour and the channel count which is not drawn, and the colour separating cleanly inside a row is
the figure's central claim seen at one noise level: at one measured tau_int the distortion still
differs between sampling rates, which is why the reader needs a second number.
Across rows it shows what the noise actually does, which is to slide the whole sweep toward
tau_int = 1: at high noise the least-squares residual is white because the instrument, not the
gating, dominates it, and every member is then calibrated for a reason that has nothing to do with
the likelihood. The top rows are where the family separates and the bottom rows are where nothing
does, and that is worth being able to see, since a reader whose recording is instrument-dominated
gets the same error bar from any member of the ladder.

AND THE ROWS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT OF THE CHANNEL COUNT THEY DO NOT DRAW. Measured in the collapse
chunk of figure_5_Nch.Rmd: the noise and the channel count enter only through r = S_tilde/N_ch, so
moving down one row is the same operation as multiplying the patch size by ten. The last table below
shows it without being asked to: the spread across the four members reads 5.64, 5.83, 5.71 and 5.75
along the diagonal (S_tilde, N_ch) = (0.01, 10), (0.1, 100), (1, 10^3), (10, 10^4), which is one
value of r drawn four times. So a reader who wants the noise axis alone must hold the channel count
fixed, and this figure does not do that. It is the reason the body figure puts the SAMPLING INTERVAL
on the rows and not this: the interval is the one design axis that does not collapse into the others.

Shares every number with figure_5.Rmd: same source files, same anchor (pool), same four members,
same shared axes. Do not re-derive anything here; if the data block has to change, change it there
first. Labels follow figure_4.Rmd:329.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r data}
source("noise_units.R")  # the one definition of S_tilde and of when to convert

SRC <- "../figure_4_source_data"
rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(SRC, f), skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_INR = "INR", macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
KEEP <- names(LAB)

# strip labels: plain from 0.01 to 100, powers outside; parsed as plotmath below.
pw10 <- function(x) {
  e <- round(log10(x))
  ifelse(abs(e) <= 2, format(x, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE), sprintf("10^%d", e))
}

tau <- rd("figure_4_source_data_cell_scalars.csv") %>%
  filter(param == "lag", anchor == "pool", algo == "nonlinearsqr") %>%
  transmute(noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, tau_int = v)

spec <- rd("figure_4_source_data_spectrum.csv") %>%
  filter(anchor == "pool", algo %in% KEEP) %>%
  select(algo, param, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, values_from = m)

dat <- spec %>%
  inner_join(tau, by = c("noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mag), is.finite(aniso), mag > 0, aniso > 0) %>%
  mutate(lo = mag / aniso, hi = mag * aniso,
         member = factor(unname(LAB[algo]), levels = unname(LAB)),
         d = factor(sprintf("%g", interval_in_tau),
                    levels = sprintf("%g", sort(unique(interval_in_tau)))),
         # the label is TEN TIMES S_tilde; convert here because this is where it is shown.
         S = dimensionless_noise(as.numeric(noise)),
         s_strip = factor(sprintf("widetilde(S) == %s", pw10(S)),
                          levels = sprintf("widetilde(S) == %s", pw10(sort(unique(S))))))

cat(sprintf("figure_5_noise: %d marks over %d cells in %d panels; per member: %s\n",
            nrow(dat), n_distinct(dat[c("noise","Num_ch","interval_in_tau")]),
            nlevels(dat$member) * nlevels(dat$s_strip),
            paste(sprintf("%s=%d", levels(dat$member), as.integer(table(dat$member))),
                  collapse = " ")))
cat("marks per row and member (the staircase of the battery):\n")
dat %>% count(s_strip, name = "marks") %>%
  mutate(per_member = marks / nlevels(dat$member),
         channel_counts = sapply(levels(s_strip), function(l)
           n_distinct(dat$Num_ch[dat$s_strip == l]))) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print()
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 8.6}
g <- ggplot(dat, aes(tau_int, mag, colour = d)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(s_strip ~ member, labeller = labeller(s_strip = label_parsed)) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10), labels = c("1", "2", "5", "10")) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100),
                labels = c("0.3", "1", "3", "10", "30", "100")) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = expression(widetilde(Delta)), option = "D", end = 0.92) +
  labs(x = expression("memory left in the least-squares residual,  "*tau[int]),
       y = "distortion of the reported information\n(point = size, bar = across directions)") +
  # sizes written out rather than left to base_size: eLife's 7 pt floor is on the drawn text.
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 7))

ggsave("Figure_5_noise.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 8.6, device = cairo_pdf)
g
```

```{r numbers}
dat %>% group_by(member, S) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), tau_med = median(tau_int), tau_max = max(tau_int),
            size_med = median(mag), size_max = max(mag),
            frac_ge_115 = mean(mag >= 1.15), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nwhere the family stops separating: spread of the size ACROSS the four members, within a cell,\n",
    "as a max/min ratio, summarised per noise level:\n", sep = "")
dat %>% group_by(S, Num_ch, interval_in_tau) %>%
  summarise(spread = max(mag) / min(mag), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  summarise(med_spread = median(spread), max_spread = max(spread), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
```
